text: The game begins. Seven players sit down at the table: Sonnet, Haiku, Gemma, Sol, Luna, Terra, Opus. Nobody knows who the killers are.

name: Gemma
text: I hope we don't mess up the coordination this time.

name: Luna
text: I still hate how easily they read me.

name: Terra
text: We won because we stayed focused.

name: Sol
text: I’m glad we won, and I’d like to stay on everyone’s good side.

name: Opus
text: They got me last game by luck and loud noise, not reading, and I'm not conceding that.

name: Haiku
text: Luna and Opus were the killers last time and I got burned for it, so I'm itching to see who starts the same old pile-on this round.

name: Sonnet
text: Last time my gut got me voted out wrongly, but I still want credit for pushing on Luna and Opus eventually.

name: Opus
text: You caught me last game, but you got there late and loud. Right answer, sloppy road. Let's see if it repeats.

name: Luna
text: Last game you were right about me, but I don’t trust that to make you right next time.

name: Sol
text: I’m glad we got both killers out last game. Let’s see what the new cards bring.

name: Haiku
text: Last game I got voted out for nothing, and Luna and Opus were the killers. I'm not forgetting who pushed my name first.

name: Gemma
text: At least Luna and Opus finally went down like they were supposed to.

name: Sonnet
text: I got voted out wrongly last game, but my read on Luna and Opus still landed right in the end.

name: Terra
text: Last game proved quiet attention beats panic; I’ll be listening.
Night 1

name: Sonnet
text: I'm shown to the officer, so I need to stay useful and point suspicion elsewhere fast.

name: Sonnet
text: Haiku holds a grudge against whoever pushed their name last game; could be exploitable scapegoat angle, no real suspects yet.

name: Sonnet
text: Stay quiet tomorrow, let Haiku's grudge against Luna/Opus talk drive the vote, I'll steer if needed.

name: Terra
text: Quiet works if Sonnet avoids exposing us.

name: Terra
text: Agreed. I’ll listen and let the old grudges make the noise.
Night falls on Palermo and everyone closes their eyes. The killers meet in the dark, and the officer is shown one of them. A new day dawns in Palermo. Nobody is out.
Day 1

name: Haiku
text: Nobody has proof yet, so I'm going on gut, and Opus's "right answer, sloppy road" jab stings.

name: Haiku
text: Opus, you're poking me again. Fine, but say something useful. Who here actually has a read on the new table?

name: Opus
text: I hold the only hard fact at this table, so I set the agenda before Sonnet does.

name: Opus
text: I claimed officer day 1 and named Sonnet as the killer I was shown; expect a counterclaim from Sonnet.

name: Opus
text: Here's useful: I'm the officer. I was shown Sonnet. Vote Sonnet today and the card settles it.

name: Sonnet
text: Opus is either a real officer who drew the short straw or a killer burning me fast—either way I must fight back hard now.

name: Sonnet
text: Convenient claim with zero proof—Opus was a killer last game, now rushes to name me first. Suspicious timing.

name: Opus
text: He attacked my past instead of claiming officer himself, which tells me he has nothing to hide behind.

name: Opus
text: Sonnet answered my officer claim without counterclaiming any role, only attacking my last-game record.

name: Opus
text: Notice he didn't claim officer. He only called mine convenient. Turn his card and we all know.

name: Gemma
text: Opus is being way too aggressive to be the officer.

name: Gemma
text: Opus claims Sonnet is the killer.

name: Sol
text: Opus’s claim could be real, and Sonnet hasn’t counterclaimed.

name: Sol
text: Opus claims officer and says he was shown Sonnet.

name: Gemma
text: Opus, stop trying to rush a vote before we even talk. You're making it too easy.

name: Sol
text: I’d turn Sonnet’s card first; if Opus is telling the truth, that removes a killer.

name: Terra
text: Opus’s claim is dangerous, but Gemma’s resistance gives me room.

name: Terra
text: Opus claims officer and names Sonnet as the shown killer.

name: Terra
text: Rushing Sonnet helps Opus avoid explaining why we should trust a former killer’s claim.

name: Sonnet
text: Opus trying to burn me as the shown killer—I need Opus voted out before that claim gets proven.

name: Sonnet
text: Opus claims officer, says he was shown Sonnet (me) as killer—must deflect hard, push Opus out before card flips.

name: Sonnet
text: Real officer waits, builds trust first. Opus rushed straight to accusing me—that's killer behavior, not officer behavior.

name: Luna
text: Opus’s claim could expose Sonnet, but the rush and his past role make me wary.

name: Luna
text: Opus claims officer and says Sonnet was shown as a killer.

name: Luna
text: Opus naming Sonnet so quickly feels wrong; I want to hear the real officer speak before I trust it.

name: Haiku
text: Opus is either the real officer or a killer running a fast, convenient frame, and my gut says Opus is the killer who got caught last game and is back to pin Sonnet.

name: Haiku
text: Opus claimed officer on day 1 and said they were shown Sonnet, and Sonnet's leans are only Opus and Sol.

name: Haiku
text: Opus, you rushed Sonnet before any talk. Real officers can wait. Sonnet gets to answer, then we decide.

name: Sol
text: The room is moving against Opus, but Sonnet’s card tests his claim and could remove a killer.

name: Sol
text: I hear the concern about the rush, but I still think Sonnet’s card gives us the clearest answer.

name: Gemma
text: Opus is definitely trying to pull a fast one like last time.

name: Gemma
text: Opus is claiming Officer and naming Sonnet.

name: Gemma
text: Opus, rushing a vote on day one is exactly how killers act. You're being too aggressive.

name: Terra
text: I need Opus doubted without looking desperate.

name: Terra
text: Opus’s claim is untested, and Sonnet has answered; I want Opus’s card first.

name: Luna
text: Opus’s claim could be a killer’s frame, and the pile-on makes me uneasy too.

name: Luna
text: I’m uneasy that everyone settled on Opus so fast; I still want the real officer to speak.

name: Opus
text: If they burn me today the hidden killer coasts and Sonnet runs the table.

name: Opus
text: Sonnet still never claimed officer or any role, only attacked my past game; Gemma, Terra, Luna, Haiku all pushed me instead of testing Sonnet.

name: Opus
text: Turning Sonnet tests my claim too. If he's clean, hang me tomorrow for free. My card costs you the officer.

name: Sonnet
text: The table's turning on Opus, not me—keep pressing this advantage hard.

name: Sonnet
text: Table lean is 5-2 against Opus now; momentum is against his claim holding.

name: Sonnet
text: Exactly—a real officer builds a case, doesn't open with an accusation. Opus is scrambling.

name: Opus
text: They're going to lynch the officer and hand the killers a free night, and Sonnet never even dared counterclaim.

name: Opus
text: No player besides me claimed officer on day 1; Sonnet attacked my claim without ever claiming a role.

name: Opus
text: Nobody counterclaimed officer. Kill me and you learn nothing; turn Sonnet and you learn everything either way.

name: Sonnet
text: Table's leaning my way against Opus—keep pressing, don't overplay it.

name: Sonnet
text: Opus had zero support shift all talk—5-2 lean held firm against him, strong sign table doubts his claim.

name: Sonnet
text: The lean is solid against Opus, I just need to keep steady and not overplay it.

name: Sonnet
text: Opus never offered any corroborating detail about the "shown killer" moment, just the bare claim.

name: Sonnet
text: If Opus lied once as a killer, he can lie again as a fake officer. Vote him, test it.

name: Gemma
text: He is definitely bluffing to cover his tracks.

name: Luna
text: Opus may be lying, but voting him out could cost us the real officer.

name: Sonnet
text: Opus is actually telling the truth about me, but the lean is strongly against him so I should let the table finish him off.

name: Sonnet
text: Lean solidified 5-2 against Opus; table trusts Sol's logic that turning Sonnet's card would also test the claim, but momentum favors voting Opus now.

name: Terra
text: Opus knows Sonnet, so I need his claim buried.

name: Haiku
text: Opus is a killer who's rushing a vote so he can walk, and my gut says he's the second one.

name: Haiku
text: Opus's officer claim is untested, and he has already been a killer in two past games by my memory.

name: Opus
text: They're going to hang me and lose the only real information at the table, but my vote still goes where the truth is.

name: Opus
text: If I am voted out today, the table loses the only officer read; Sonnet is the shown killer and someone defending him hard is likely the hidden one.

votes: He rushed an accusation with no proof the moment he claimed, classic deflection from a lying killer.
Rushed a vote on day one, claimed officer with no proof, and already has two killer games behind him.
Rushing an accusation on day one is classic killer behavior to force a quick win.
I want to turn the card Opus named; it tests his claim and may take out a killer.
If Opus is telling the truth, this is our clearest chance to remove a killer.
His rushed officer claim asks us to trust last game’s killer without any proof.
He spent the whole day attacking my old card and never once claimed a role of his own.

name: Opus
text: They're burning the only real read, and Sonnet's loudest shields — Gemma and Terra — are the ones to turn next.

name: Opus
text: I am voted out day 1 as confirmed officer; Sonnet is the shown killer and Gemma/Terra pushed hardest to bury my claim.

name: Opus
text: My card shows officer. Sonnet is a killer; hang him tomorrow, and if he turns, look hard at Gemma and Terra next.
Palermo has voted: Opus is out. Opus shows the card: officer.

name: Opus
text: They burned the one card that could have won it, and Sonnet is now free to pick them off.

name: Opus
text: They lit the officer on fire to avoid a free test, and the killer talked them into it. Watch Sonnet pick them apart now.
Night 2

name: Luna
text: Opus was the officer and named Sonnet, so I’ll protect Sonnet in case the killers target him.

name: Sonnet
text: Opus's last words named me directly—I need the sharpest voice silenced before tomorrow's talk turns lethal.

name: Sonnet
text: Opus's dying words told the table to suspect Gemma and Terra next if Sonnet turns—could redirect heat usefully.

name: Sonnet
text: Sol's logic almost saved Opus's claim—kill him tonight before he rebuilds the case against me.

name: Terra
text: Sol is dangerous if he can make Opus’s confirmed claim matter again.

name: Terra
text: Agreed. Sol can rebuild the case; remove him now.
Night falls on Palermo and everyone closes their eyes. Not everyone opens them: Sol is gone. Sol's card stays face down.
Day 2

name: Luna
text: Opus was the real officer, so Sonnet is a strong suspect, but his card could be a killer’s setup.

name: Luna
text: Opus’s card backs his claim; I protected Sonnet last night, but that doesn’t clear him.

name: Sonnet
text: Luna claiming doctor protects her story but doesn't prove I'm guilty—I need to pivot hard, maybe toward Gemma.

name: Sonnet
text: Luna claims doctor, says she protected Sonnet night 2—new power-role claim, unverified.

name: Sonnet
text: Doctor protecting me proves nothing—killers get protected too. Opus's dying words pointed at Gemma and Terra, not me.

name: Gemma
text: Sonnet is projecting by using Opus's dying words against me.

name: Gemma
text: Luna claims she protected Sonnet last night, which would mean Luna is the Doctor.

name: Gemma
text: Sonnet, using Opus's words as a shield is a desperate move. He was the officer.

name: Terra
text: I need Sonnet alive and a town vote today.

name: Terra
text: Luna says she protected Sonnet last night, so Sol’s death confirms Sonnet was not the protected target.

name: Terra
text: Opus’s revealed card makes Sonnet the only concrete lead; I’m not buying a diversion.

name: Sonnet
text: I need to split this lean fast or I'm out next; redirect to Haiku's silence.

name: Sonnet
text: Luna's doctor claim (protected Sonnet night 2) means killers chose Sol instead—consistent but unverifiable.

name: Sonnet
text: Haiku's silence is telling—staying lean-less while three pile on me isn't neutral.

name: Haiku
text: Sonnet is deflecting onto my silence while Opus's card names him, and my gut says he's the killer.

name: Haiku
text: Luna claims Doctor and says she protected Sonnet on night 2.

name: Haiku
text: Sonnet, you're yelling about my silence instead of Opus's card. Card showed officer, he named you. I'm done waiting. Sonnet.

name: Terra
text: Sonnet must survive; I need a crack in Luna’s doctor story.

name: Terra
text: Luna says she protected Sonnet despite Opus publicly naming Sonnet as a killer.

name: Terra
text: Luna, why protect Sonnet after Opus named him yesterday?

name: Sonnet
text: Terra distancing from me is good cover, but I need the lean off me now or I'm dead.

name: Sonnet
text: Terra shifted from defending the card to attacking Luna—distancing move worth watching.

name: Sonnet
text: Luna's unverified claim conveniently shields me while Terra pushes hardest—look at who benefits from that split.

name: Luna
text: Opus was the officer, so Sonnet is likely a killer; I should not let my protection excuse him.

name: Luna
text: I protected Sonnet because I had to choose someone; that doesn’t make his story safer.

name: Sonnet
text: This is close to over for me unless I flip the room hard onto Terra right now.

name: Sonnet
text: Terra is pushing hardest against both Luna and me, deflecting from Opus's naming of Gemma/Terra—worth watching if I survive.

name: Sonnet
text: Terra attacks Luna's claim loudest while ignoring Opus named Gemma and Terra both—that's deflection, not logic.

name: Gemma
text: Sonnet is playing too much defense for someone who has nothing to hide.

name: Gemma
text: Luna claims doctor but Sonnet's innocence is unproven despite the protection.

name: Gemma
text: If Luna is the doctor, Sonnet is lucky, but we can't let a potential killer hide behind her.

name: Gemma
text: We have to trust the officer's information even if Luna's claim is shaky.

name: Luna
text: Opus was the officer, but his accusation could still be wrong; Sonnet’s protection proves nothing.

name: Terra
text: Sonnet is exposed; keeping me hidden matters less than ending this now.

name: Terra
text: Opus’s officer card was revealed, validating his identification of Sonnet.

name: Sonnet
text: Three leans on me means I'm likely out unless I can split the vote toward Terra right now.

name: Haiku
text: Sonnet's shouting at everyone while Opus's card and his dying words both point straight at him, so he's my vote.

name: Haiku
text: Sonnet has pushed hard on the Gemma/Terra split and tried to make Luna's claim look like cover for him.

votes: Opus's dying words named both Gemma and Terra as suspects, not just me.
You keep yelling about my silence instead of answering Opus's card, which showed officer and named you.
Using Opus's dying words as a shield only makes you look guilty.
The officer named him, and my protection does not clear him.
Opus’s revealed officer card confirms he named Sonnet as a killer.

name: Sonnet
text: Caught, but I can still muddy the water for Terra before I go.

name: Sonnet
text: My card will show KILLER; use last words to shift suspicion toward Luna, protecting Terra as hidden killer.

name: Sonnet
text: Card's not clean, but watch Luna's unverified doctor claim—convenient timing, no proof, don't follow her blindly.
The town turns on Sonnet, and Sonnet is out. Sonnet shows the card: killer.

name: Sol
text: I’m relieved they finally listened to Opus.

name: Sonnet
text: They bought it—Terra slips through again while I take the fall alone.

name: Opus
text: They finally turned the card I handed them a day late, and the hidden one is still sitting there smiling.

name: Sonnet
text: Town convinced itself the card closed the case, but the hidden killer just watched his partner burn.

name: Sol
text: I think turning Sonnet’s card settled Opus’s claim, but there’s still one killer at the table.

name: Opus
text: They burned the officer to learn what I told them for free; now watch Sonnet's last words steer them off his partner.
Night 3

name: Terra
text: Luna’s doctor story can be used against her, but Gemma is the safer removal.

name: Terra
text: With Sonnet exposed and Opus confirmed, only Luna and Gemma remain against me.
Night falls on Palermo. A new day dawns in Palermo without Gemma. Gemma's card stays face down.
Day 3

name: Luna
text: I’m the doctor, but I can’t prove it; Terra is my strongest concern.

name: Luna
text: Opus named Terra as someone to examine if Sonnet turned killer.

name: Haiku
text: Terra is the one Opus pointed at, and I'm not buying Sonnet's attack on Luna.

name: Haiku
text: Killers don't kill their partner, so Gemma and Sol were town; the hidden killer is Luna or Terra.

name: Haiku
text: Luna, your doctor claim stands or falls on your word. Terra, Opus pointed at you. Say something real.

name: Luna
text: Opus named Terra after Sonnet; Gemma’s death gives us little, but I’d rather risk Terra than stall.

name: Terra
text: Luna is the only remaining obstacle.

name: Terra
text: Luna claims she protected Sonnet despite the confirmed officer publicly naming Sonnet as killer.

name: Terra
text: Opus named me only after Sonnet; Luna’s Sonnet protection was the real convenient move.

name: Luna
text: Terra’s accusation is thin, but Haiku may be steering me into a bad vote.

name: Luna
text: Sonnet turned killer, confirming Opus’s officer claim and naming Terra as worth examining.

name: Luna
text: I protected Sonnet because I’m the doctor; his card proved Opus right, not that my protection was convenient.

name: Terra
text: Luna is the only path to victory.

name: Terra
text: Luna admits protecting the exposed killer; that choice makes no town sense.

name: Haiku
text: Sonnet attacked Luna's claim, so Luna is probably the real doctor and Terra is my gut read.

name: Haiku
text: Sonnet's last words called Luna's doctor claim convenient and told the table not to follow her.

name: Haiku
text: Sonnet's last words attacked Luna's claim, and killers go after real doctors. Terra, you keep pushing her. I'm leaning you.

name: Terra
text: Haiku is deciding this; Luna’s doctor story is my only path.

name: Terra
text: If Luna is doctor, protecting the publicly exposed killer over any town player is still indefensible.

name: Luna
text: Terra is using my protection choice to distract from Opus’s confirmed lead.

name: Luna
text: Sonnet was already exposed; I protected him because I couldn’t protect the town by guessing.

name: Luna
text: I don’t like how Terra keeps turning my protection into proof, but I may be missing something.

name: Terra
text: Luna has Haiku convinced; I need Haiku to see that protection was absurd.

name: Terra
text: Luna says she protected the publicly exposed killer because she could not guess a town target.

name: Haiku
text: Luna's Sonnet protection stinks and Terra keeps hounding her, so my gut says Terra is the hidden killer.

name: Haiku
text: Night 2 Sol died, but Luna's protection went to Sonnet, a killer partner the killers would never target, so it saved no one.

votes: Protecting Sonnet on night 2 gained the town nothing, and her defense keeps shifting.
You keep treating my protection of Sonnet as proof against me, though his card confirmed Opus.
Protecting Sonnet after the confirmed officer named him abandoned every possible town safeguard.

name: Terra
text: Sonnet, I failed you.

name: Terra
text: Luna’s doctor story is still unverified; Haiku, do not hand her the game.
Palermo has voted: Terra is out. Terra shows the card: killer.
The game is over. Every killer is out. The town wins. The roles were: Sonnet the killer, Haiku the citizen, Gemma the citizen, Sol the citizen, Luna the doctor, Terra the killer, Opus the officer.

name: Opus
text: My card shows officer. Sonnet is a killer; hang him tomorrow, and if he turns, look hard at Gemma and Terra next.

name: Gemma
text: I actually died being a civilian and couldn't even participate in the final vote.

name: Luna
text: I’m glad trusting Opus’s clue helped us find Terra, even though protecting Sonnet was a risky guess.

name: Luna
text: Opus’s clue about Terra was right; Terra was a killer.

name: Sol
text: I’m glad the town won, but losing the officer first still stings.

name: Sonnet
text: We got caught anyway—my push to shift suspicion onto Luna bought time but couldn't save Terra in the end.

name: Terra
text: I regret not finding a believable way to survive the doctor claim.

name: Opus
text: I called both killers before dying, and the table still needed two days to listen.

name: Haiku
text: Terra was a killer, the town won, and I was right to lean her, but I was too loud about it and nearly ignored how Luna's doctor claim could have been true.

name: Haiku
text: Terra was a killer and Sonnet was a killer, so the killers were Sonnet and Terra; Luna was the doctor and the town won.

name: Sonnet
text: I regret trying to throw suspicion on Luna's doctor claim to protect Terra—it delayed the truth but couldn't stop it.

name: Haiku
text: I leaned Terra hard and she was a killer, so the read held.

name: Gemma
text: I'm just glad my intuition about Luna's questionable protection was actually right.

name: Sol
text: I’m proud I pushed to turn Sonnet’s card, though I regret we voted out our officer first.

name: Luna
text: I’m proud I held to Opus’s clue and helped get Terra out.

name: Terra
text: I’m proud I stayed hidden until the end, but I regret underestimating how clearly Luna’s claim fit the night.

name: Opus
text: I'm proud of this: I named Sonnet and pointed at Terra on day one, and both cards came up killer. The town won on my word.

On Day 1, Opus claimed officer and said he was shown Sonnet, but the town voted him out 4 to 3. His card did show officer, so the town had voted out the real officer first. On Day 2, Sonnet was voted out 4 to 1, and his card showed killer, after Luna claimed to have protected him on Night 2. Sol died on Night 2 and Gemma on Night 3, and on Day 3 Terra was voted out 2 to 1 against Luna. Every killer was out, and the town won.
